children: The National Stock Exchange (NSE) has announced the inclusion of Acutaas Chemicals Ltd. and Apar Industries Ltd. in its futures and options (F&O) segment, with trading in derivative contracts on the two stocks set to begin on Wednesday, November 25.
The exchange has fixed the market lot at 150 shares for Acutaas Chemicals and 50 shares for Apar Industries.

The addition of the two stocks comes alongside changes to the exchange's derivatives segment, with Indian Energy Exchange (IEX) and Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency (IREDA) set to exit the F&O segment this month.

The inclusion of a stock in the derivatives segment allows traders to take positions through futures and options contracts linked to the underlying shares. The stocks continue to remain available for regular trading in the cash market.
On Monday, shares of Acutaas Chemicals rose 0.52% to close at ₹3,851, while Apar Industries declined 1.12% to settle at ₹14,174.40.
Over the past year, Acutaas Chemicals has gained 116%, while Apar Industries has advanced nearly 60%.
Key triggers for the December series
The December derivatives series will be the final monthly series of 2026, with market participants tracking a range of domestic and global cues.
Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) continued to remain net buyers on Monday, while their cumulative inflows for November crossed $14 billion, according to the market update.
The following key triggers are likely to influence market sentiment during the December series:
- RBI monetary policy: The Reserve Bank of India's policy decision on December 4.
- US Federal Reserve policy: The US Fed's decision on December 8.
- Budget-related developments: Newsflow and expectations ahead of the Union Budget.
- Crude oil prices: Movements in oil prices and their implications for inflation and the rupee.
- Bond yields: Changes in global and domestic yields, which could influence equity market sentiment.
Market participants will also track FII flows and broader global cues as the December series begins.

title: December F&O Series: Two new stocks enter the segment; IREDA, IEX to exit
